issues.description: Inconsistent method naming for the meal-price calculation across artifacts: the problem statement and UML require a method named calculateTotalPrice(Meal), the template Main and solution SealSaloon provide/expect a method named computeMealCost(Meal), while the solution Main calls calculateTotalPrice(Meal). This signature/name mismatch will confuse students about which method to implement and call, and may cause compilation errors or failing tests depending on which name is used.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the meal-price method name consistent across all artifacts. Rename computeMealCost(Meal) in code to calculateTotalPrice(Meal) (and update all callers), or update the problem statement/UML to specify computeMealCost(Meal). Ensure both the SealSaloon class and any example Main code use the same static method name.

issues.description: The problem statement specifies a static method named calculateTotalPrice(Meal) to compute a meal's total cost, but the codebase uses a different identifier (computeMealCost) for the same concept. Template/Main and SealSaloon implementations call/define computeMealCost, while the UML/problem text and one Main variant reference calculateTotalPrice. This inconsistent naming for the single conceptual operation (compute the total price of a Meal) creates confusion about which method students should implement or call and may cause mismatches between tests, instructions, and example code.
issues.suggestedFix: Standardize the method name for computing a meal's total price across all artifacts. For example, rename computeMealCost to calculateTotalPrice in SealSaloon and update all calls (and example Main) to use calculateTotalPrice, or alternatively update the problem statement/UML to use computeMealCost—choose one consistent identifier and apply it everywhere.
